sources.citation: Jergas, H., & Baethge, C. (2015). Quotation accuracy in medical journal articles: A systematic review and meta-analysis. PeerJ, 3, e1364.

sources.title: The Essential Impact of Context on Organizational Behavior
sources.citation: Johns, G. (2006). The Essential Impact of Context on Organizational Behavior. Academy of Management Review, 31(2), 386-408.

concepts.locator: abstract; https://www.jstor.org/stable/20159208
concepts.relationship: Does not mean every sentence must name a contextual moderator.

sources.title: Editor's Comments: Publishing Theory
sources.citation: Kilduff, M. (2006). Editor's Comments: Publishing Theory. Academy of Management Review, 31(2), 252-255.

concepts.paraphrase: Notes that formal propositions suit some approaches to theory, while theoretical approaches vary. Supports treating propositions as optional genre devices.
concepts.locator: discussion of propositions and different theoretical approaches
concepts.relationship: Does not require propositions or establish a universal paper template.

sources.title: Recognizing speculative language in biomedical research articles: A linguistically motivated perspective
sources.citation: Kilicoglu, H., & Bergler, S. (2008). Recognizing speculative language in biomedical research articles: A linguistically motivated perspective. Proceedings of BioNLP 2008, 46-53.

concepts.locator: PDF p. 1; hedging can alter factual status and same word is context-dependent
concepts.relationship: Biomedical corpus and speculation recognition do not determine whether an argument is adequately qualified. Motivates the criterion or distinction only; it does not prove this harness's rule wording, semantic judgments, or checker accuracy.

sources.title: Toward a model of text comprehension and production
sources.citation: Kintsch, W., & van Dijk, T. A. (1978). Toward a model of text comprehension and production. Psychological Review, 85(5), 363-394.

concepts.paraphrase: The model distinguishes local semantic connections from global gist and explains how a reader constructs a coherent text base. This motivates attention to hierarchy and paragraph coherence, but does not mandate headings, one-point paragraphs, or topic-first placement.
concepts.locator: p. 363 abstract and introduction; pp. 365-366 semantic macrostructure and schematic structure
concepts.relationship: ['Original facsimile hosted by a university course rather than current publisher; source supports a comprehension model, not a checker threshold.']

concepts.paraphrase: The model distinguishes local links among propositions from a discourse-wide topic and treats both local connection and global organization as aspects of coherence. Readers can infer some links, so an unstated step is not automatically absent from understanding.
concepts.locator: Printed pp. 365-366; PDF pages 2-3, Semantic Structures and Macrostructure of Discourse.
concepts.relationship: This is a theory of comprehension and production, not a mandate for heading order, topic-first prose, or the staged checker's exact up/down tests. The mapping is background for relating parts to a whole.

sources.title: Editors' comments: Sense and structure - The core building blocks of an AMR article

concepts.locator: printed p. 407 (PDF p. 1), opening and five-block introduction
concepts.relationship: AMR editorial guidance; not a mandatory format for every genre or a validation of checker flags.

sources.title: Strategies for Theorizing from Process Data
sources.citation: Langley, A. (1999). Strategies for Theorizing from Process Data. Academy of Management Review, 24(4), 691-710.

concepts.relationship: Data-analysis advice does not establish that a prose checker can assess empirical truth.

concepts.relationship: Does not imply that every theory must model temporality or linear stages.

sources.title: Automatically evaluating text coherence using discourse relations
sources.citation: Lin, Z., Ng, H. T., & Kan, M.-Y. (2011). Automatically evaluating text coherence using discourse relations. Proceedings of ACL-HLT 2011, 997-1006.

concepts.locator: Publisher-indexed abstract only; no printed passage locator.
concepts.relationship: This is a study of contribution construction, not evidence that every current draft must challenge an assumption; no current rule support asserted.

sources.citation: MacInnis, D. J. (2011). A Framework for Conceptual Contributions in Marketing. Journal of Marketing, 75(4), 136-154.

concepts.relationship: Marketing-specific contribution taxonomy; current core deliberately excludes novelty and importance judgments.

concepts.locator: passage on articulating and justifying assumptions and translating causal logic
concepts.relationship: Formal modeling outlet advice does not impose mathematics or a prose format on other genres.

sources.title: Optimizing concepts: Conceptual engineering in the field of management - The case of routines research
sources.citation: Makowski, P. T. (2021). Optimizing concepts: Conceptual engineering in the field of management - The case of routines research. Academy of Management Review, 46(4), 702-724.

sources.title: Conceptual engineering: The assessment of rigor and rudimentary recommendations for theory developers

concepts.paraphrase: In response to Oswick and colleagues, Makowski argues for making conceptual innovations and updates reflective and explicit while considering conceptual precision and rigor.
concepts.locator: dialogue manuscript opening (PDF p. 3)
concepts.relationship: A contested methodological position; do not present the exchange as settled proof of a harness rule.

sources.title: Rhetorical Structure Theory: Toward a functional theory of text organization
sources.citation: Mann, W. C., & Thompson, S. A. (1988). Rhetorical Structure Theory: Toward a functional theory of text organization. Text, 8(3), 243-281.

concepts.paraphrase: Parts of a coherent text can have recognizable functions relative to other parts, including evidence, background, elaboration, contrast, and condition; span order is not fixed and more than one plausible analysis may exist.
concepts.locator: RST development-team Introduction to RST, sections 'Texts, Coherence and Structure' and 'Nucleus::Satellite Relations'; no original article page claimed.
concepts.relationship: Conceptual background from the developer site, not a page-level check of the 1988 article. It does not impose a mandatory heading hierarchy, unique reading, or automatic failure for a span without a detected relation.

sources.title: Configurational approaches to organizational analysis

sources.title: Developing Theory about the Development of Theory
sources.citation: Mintzberg, H. (2014, January). Developing theory about the development of theory. Author revision of the 2005 chapter in Great Minds in Management, pp. 355-372.

concepts.relationship: Related counterweight to rigid model format, not a proof of a diagnostic.

concepts.locator: 2014 author version pp. 3-4, 'What Theory Development Isn't'
concepts.relationship: Background for distinguishing reported material, inference, and testing; author's methodological view.

sources.title: Building Better Theory: Time and the Specification of When Things Happen

concepts.locator: abstract; https://www.jstor.org/stable/3560240
concepts.relationship: Timing questions apply when temporality matters; no universal time-variable requirement follows.

concepts.locator: dialogue manuscript p. 2 (PDF p. 3), 'Idea Generation in Abductive Thinking'
concepts.relationship: A debate about generating theory; it should not become a mandatory checker taxonomy.

sources.title: The Challenges of Building Theory by Combining Lenses
sources.citation: Okhuysen, G.; Bonardi, J. P. (2011). The Challenges of Building Theory by Combining Lenses. Academy of Management Review, 36(1), 6-11.

concepts.locator: discussion of conceptual proximity between lenses
concepts.relationship: Does not require an outside lens or any fixed number of lenses.

sources.title: Concept Fallibility in Organizational Science
sources.citation: Osigweh, C. A. B. (1989). Concept Fallibility in Organizational Science. Academy of Management Review, 14(4), 579-594.

concepts.relationship: Conceptual rigor is broader than detecting term repetition or synonym changes.

concepts.locator: abstract, https://www.jstor.org/stable/259350
concepts.relationship: Narrative is one theory form; deeper structure is not an obligatory causal arrow in every paper.

sources.citation: Poole, M. S.; van de Ven, A. H. (1989). Using Paradox to Build Management and Organization Theories. Academy of Management Review, 14(4), 562-578.

concepts.locator: abstract, https://www.jstor.org/stable/258559
concepts.relationship: Does not mean every tension is a defect or must be eliminated.

sources.citation: Ragins, B. R. (2012). Editor's Comments: Reflections on the Craft of Clear Writing. Academy of Management Review, 37(4), 493-501.

sources.title: Analyzing the past to prepare for the future: Writing a literature review
